thread.title: Global stocks slump as Apple outlook weighs on investors

author: Bloomberg News
title: Global stocks slump as Apple outlook weighs on investors
text:
European stocks and U.S. equity-index futures slumped after Apple Inc. ( AAPL.O ) added to global growth concerns with a cut in its sales outlook. Stocks in Asia were mixed, while there were wild moves in the currency markets as the yen surged.
Technology shares led the Stoxx Europe 600 Index lower after the maker of iPhones cut its first-quarter guidance for the first time in almost two decades, citing an unforeseen slowdown in China and fewer upgrades to its flagship mobile device. Contracts on the Nasdaq index led the drop for U.S. futures, dipping as much as 2.9 per cent. In currency markets, the yen jumped and the Australian dollar slumped to the lowest in almost 10 years as algorithmic programs amplified sharp gyrations amid thin liquidity during a Japanese holiday. Treasuries declined along with most European bonds.
Investors attempting to turn the page on 2018 are finding the same old issues spoiling the mood. While fundamentals appear strong by some measures, the protectionist showdown is starting to have an impact on economic activity, as demonstrated by Apple’s warning and a weak reading on Chinese manufacturing. Dysfunction in Washington continues, meanwhile, with leaders unable to strike a deal to end a partial shutdown of the federal government.
“That Tim Cook and his company mentioned China as the reason behind the downturn in the company’s outlook seemed to hit exactly the pressure point traders and investors were already alarmed over,” Greg McKenna, markets strategist at McKenna Macro and a three-decade foreign-exchange market veteran, wrote in a note to clients. “That is, the China and global slowdown which seems to have been confirmed by Wednesday’s global manufacturing PMI data.”
Elsewhere, West Texas oil again slipped to about US$46 a barrel. Gold gained a sixth day.
Here are some events investors may focus on in coming days:
The U.S. December jobs report is due Friday Fed Chair Powell is interviewed with predecessors Janet Yellen and Ben Bernanke at the annual meeting of the American Economic Association Friday. Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic joins a panel on long-run macroeconomic performance.
And these are the main moves in markets:
Stocks
The Stoxx Europe 600 Index fell 0.6 per cent as of 9:47 a.m. London time to the lowest in a week on the largest fall in a week. Futures on the S&P 500 Index sank 1.4 per cent to the lowest in more than a week on the biggest tumble in more than a week. The U.K.’s FTSE 100 Index fell 0.3 per cent to the lowest in a week. Germany’s DAX Index sank 0.8 per cent, reaching the lowest in a week. The MSCI Emerging Market Index dipped 0.5 per cent to the lowest in more than a week. The MSCI Asia Pacific Index advanced 0.3 per cent.
Currencies
The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index decreased 0.2 per cent. The euro advanced 0.3 per cent to US$1.1382, the biggest gain in a week. The British pound decreased 0.2 per cent to US$1.2581, the weakest in more than three weeks. The Japanese yen surged 1.1 per cent to 107.72 per dollar, the strongest in more than eight months on the biggest jump in two weeks.
Bonds
The yield on 10-year Treasuries jumped two basis points to 2.64 per cent, the largest surge in more than a week. Germany’s 10-year yield climbed one basis point to 0.18 per cent, the biggest surge in almost two weeks. Britain’s 10-year yield advanced one basis point to 1.224 per cent, the largest gain in a week. Italy’s 10-year yield climbed seven basis points to 2.765 per cent, the highest in more than a week on the biggest surge in almost two weeks.
Commodities
West Texas Intermediate crude decreased 0.9 per cent to US$46.11 a barrel, the first retreat in a week. Gold advanced 0.3 per cent to US$1,288.09 an ounce, reaching the highest in almost seven months on its sixth consecutive advance.
